label: Esse and proposed quiddity in a contingent conjunction
term: SCG I.22 contingent conjunction of esse and proposed quiddity, analyst profile
definition: A typed analyst profile holds a concrete bearer, the q.3 a.4 representation of its actual esse and essence as principles, a SEPARATELY NAMED proposed quiddity which may be rejected, a frame of worlds, existence of an esse principle, joining of that esse to the proposed quiddity, conceptual intelligibility apart, accidental-to-esse status, an ontic identification of the bearer with its esse, and whether the proposed q is genuinely that bearer's quiddity. Successful identity of the proposed q with the actual q.3 essence is not presumed by the proposal itself. NecessaryEsseAt means that the very same esse principle exists at the selected world and every accessible world. ContingentConjunctionAt means joined at the selected world but not joined at some accessible world. ModalSeparationAt additionally requires that the same esse still exists in the counterworld. The three premise definitions govern world-separation-to-intelligibility, intelligibility-to-accident, and accident-to-nonquiddity when the bearer is identified with esse. No relation is reducible by definition to another; none is a cause of existence, a global grounding relation, or the equality of esseOf and essenceOf.
note: Motivated by SCG I.22 n.3 and the first written case of n.4, but analyst semantics, not a certified source claim: no pinned corpus passage for these locators has yet been materialized and read. n.4 has a second written case (si autem non potest intelligi illud esse sine illa essentia: the esse then depends absolutely on whatever its conjunction depends on, returning the n.2 horns); this profile does not formalize it, and has no relation for the source on which the conjunction depends or for absolute dependence of the esse. Those relata remain an OPEN semantic obligation for the second-case slice. Sibling reading of n.3's 'non per se necesse': this profile renders it by the modal proxy (ContingentConjunctionAt, with per se necessity of esse rendered by NecessaryEsseAt). A sibling dependence sense, not yet formalized, reads per se/per aliud as whether something has a cause of its necessity, matching n.3's 'dependet quantum ad coniunctionem'; on it a conjunction present at every world but dependent satisfies n.3, and per se necesse belongs on the underived side of DISAMB-NECESSARY-EXISTENCE-VS-UNDERIVED, not on the NecessaryAt side. Scope claims made with this profile are relative to the modal proxy. The distinction between a necessary e and a contingent relation e-q is intelligible as a world-indexed assignment, but the conceptual 'can be understood apart' of n.4 is not defined by a possible-world gap. That transition is an OPEN premise. Accident means a feature adventitious relative to the bearer-identified esse, not chance occurrence or logically contingent truth; genuine quiddity is not such a feature under an additional OPEN rule. Ordinary examples of an accidental property (whiteness belonging to a human) and of a non-accidental kind (human nature) orient the distinction, but do not establish its applicability to an independently subsisting esse. No verified concrete example of a self-necessary subsistent esse is available. The predicates' transitivity, symmetry, well-foundedness, and generalization across categories of beings are unasserted. The non-esse-bearer and stable distinct-union finite controls preserve the strongest logical alternatives; they are not metaphysical possibility arguments. The intended connection is to the D-to-E root-route question in #1595 and the existing q.3 route in #319; this model rejects one contingent-attachment move without proving E.
